title: Batch Alchemy: preflight notes & microtasks
content:
Batch Alchemy — morning preflight (short form)
Date: 2025-02-12
Owner: Amir H.
Context: chasing intermittent p99 spikes on small-string generation workloads after the autoscaler bump. Today I'm focused on quick, low-friction experiments and triage steps I can run between standup and the infra sync.

TL;DR observations
- Spike pattern: p99 jumps from ~420ms to ~1.2s for 1–3 minute windows, correlated with a flurry of short requests (avg token < 12) from customer-42.
- Affected path: hosted-api -> model x86-4q -> continuous batching enabled.
- Hypothesis 1: small-request batch packing oscillates causing head-of-line delays when batch window changes.
- Hypothesis 2: KV cache population on warm workers interacts poorly with our eviction timer (gc window 15s) causing re-warm stalls.

Quick checklist (today)
- [ ] Reproduce locally: run synthetic client hitting short prompts at 150rps for 10m. Save trace.
- [ ] Add detailed batching debug logging for 2 workers (dev flags only).
- [ ] Run controlled A/B: disable prefix batching for 30m and compare tail latencies.
- [ ] Validate KV eviction counts on affected hosts (metric: kv.evictions/sec) -> escalate if > 0.5
- [ ] If stable, draft rollback playbook for continuous batching feature flag.

Commands/quick snippets (notes to self)
- Replayer load: `python tools/replay_client.py --rps 150 --prompt-file small_prompts.txt --duration 600`
- Dump batching queue state (debug endpoint): `curl -s http://worker:9100/debug/batches | jq .`
- Check KV metrics: `kubectl -n serving port-forward svc/metrics 9090:9090 && curl http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_eviction`
- Lightweight trace: start perf trace on one host: `sudo perf record -a -g -- sleep 60` then `perf script` -> flamegraph.

Hypotheses + experiments (mapped)
1) Batch window oscillation
   - Reproduce with replayer; if p99 tracks, change batch window target from 8ms -> 4ms and 16ms in 30s windows to see sensitivity.
   - If confirmed, try smoothing scheduler: moving-average of last N arrival intervals.

2) KV cache eviction causing re-warm
   - Look at kv.put/kv.get miss ratio in 1m windows during spike.
   - Toggle eviction timer from 15s -> 60s for a subset of workers (flag: RUNTIME_KV_EVICT_MS).
   - Observe memory pressure (resident set) and CPU; if memory ok and p99 improves, we need a longer-term fix.

3) Worker GC/host-level jitter
   - Correlate with node-level telemetry: CPU steal, syscalls per second, context-switch spikes.
   - Short experiment: pin test workers to isolated cores (cpuset) and see if jitter disappears.

Notes from overnight triage (copied here)
- Marcus saw two hosts (g4dn-2x) report NVLink errors around 03:12 UTC. Link to logs: GH PR thread in linked_artifacts. Not sure if correlated.
- Short requests from customer-42 started after they flipped their batching client; confirm with them whether they switched to 'send-each' mode.

Small decisions I can take now (low blast radius)
- Temporarily increase RUNTIME_KV_EVICT_MS to 45000ms for a canary pod set.
- Add 2s extra batch flush timeout for single-request batches to reduce head-of-line losses.
- If rolling, do 5 pods at a time and monitor p99.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Does our autoscaler shape request bursts in a way that interacts badly with batching? (ask infra team: Tom)
- Are there any recent kernel upgrades on the affected hosts in the last week? (check infra-ami changelog)
- What does the network latencies distribution look like for internal RPCs (between inference proxy and model workers) during spikes?

Meeting agenda (infra sync at 10:30)
- 10m: quick summary of repro attempt + immediate mitigations (canary eviction change)
- 10m: propose instrumentation change: expose per-batch age histogram + queue depth; cost estimate ~2 d-dev effort
- 5m: if we need immediate rollback plan for continuous batching, confirm rollback steps and owner

Artifacts to attach to ticket INF-2345
- Replayer command & seed used
- batch debug logs (dev only) for two workers
- flamegraph of one affected host during spike

Personal microtasks (today, personal)
- [ ] draft quick rollback doc for product (less than 1 page)
- [ ] open PR with batching debug flags and a flag gate (target branch: staging)
- [ ] sync with Marcus re NVLink logs and infra anomalies

Random heuristics / thinking aloud (brain dump)
- Small requests harm throughput because they allow the scheduler to make many micro-decisions; maybe we should special-case < 16-token requests to a fastpath that avoids continuous batching and uses immediate flush with lightweight preemption.
- Alternatively, a priority queue where requests with extremely small sequences get scheduled into a separate micro-batcher with tighter timers.

Notes-to-self: keep it short and actionable. If I can't reproduce in 45m, escalate to SRE on-call and propose the canary eviction change.

End log.
